rationale: JSONC with a hard syntax error. deacon rejects at parse; the reference uses a recovering jsonc parser that accepts and drops whatever follows the break. ADJUDICATED 2026-08-02 and kept, with the measurements folded in because the original two-line rationale asserted the conclusion without them. deacon is NOT stricter than the format, only strict about it — measured against oracle 0.87.0 on four documents: line and block comments ACCEPTED by both; a trailing comma ACCEPTED by both; `"features":` with no value REJECTED by deacon, accepted by the reference; an unclosed object REJECTED by deacon, accepted by the reference. Everything valid JSONC permits, deacon takes. WHAT ACCEPTANCE COSTS: in the `"features":` document the author wrote a `features` key, and the reference's resolved configuration reports only `name` and `image` — the Features are gone, with no diagnostic and exit 0; the unclosed document loses everything after the break the same way. deacon reports `JSONC parsing error: Unexpected close brace on line 5 column 1`. That is the same failure shape this project refused to ship in its own code the day this was adjudicated (the duplicate-Features fix was held back precisely because it silently dropped a declared Feature — see gap-features-duplicate-in-one-document), so accepting here would put deacon on both sides of constitution IV. SPEC POSITION: devcontainer-reference.md names the format — metadata 'can be stored in a JSON with Comments file called devcontainer.json' — but says nothing about a file that is not valid JSONC, so the spec is genuinely silent and the behavior's `spec: unspecified` stands. Revisit if the spec ever defines recovery semantics for a malformed configuration, at which point deacon should follow it.
